title: A film starts in the viewer's audio language
description: PlaybackInfo's DefaultAudioStreamIndex is the file's flagged track, else the first (stream.go:462), whatever the viewer's AudioLanguagePreference and PlayDefaultAudioTrack. Choose it as Jellyfin 12.4 does from the saved settings (JS-116), comparing languages as JS-117 does, with 'OriginalLanguage' meaning the film's original language.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first: compat/captures/audio-default-12.4.md and .json record DefaultAudioStreamIndex on a real Jellyfin 12.4 for at least 12 films x AudioLanguagePreference ('', eng, deu, OriginalLanguage) x PlayDefaultAudioTrack (true, false): the default flag on the first track, the second, none and all; ger and deu tags; an untagged track; two tracks in one language; a single track; and the rule that fits is written down
jellyscale answers the captured index in every cell (at least 96), except the cells listed in compat/differences.yaml with a reason
With no audio language saved, every film's default is what it is today
With JS-119's hiding on, the default is a listed Audio stream in every cell, never a placeholder

In real jellyfin-web (e2e): a viewer whose audio language is German starts a film with audio eng (default) and deu in German, with the video copied and not re-encoded; a film with only eng plays directly as before
docs/transcoding.md says that a preferred track which is not the file's default turns a browser's direct play into a copied stream, and docs/status.md marks the settings as acting

Observed first on Jellyfin 12.4: what DefaultAudioStreamIndex answers when the request names AudioStreamIndex; jellyscale then follows it (moved here from JS-119: today defaultAudio, stream.go:304, ignores the named track for every viewer)
source: Owner request 2026-11-15 ('support using the language the person has chosen for Jellyfin')
notes: Cost: a browser plays only a file's default audio track, so a different default is a copy with that track (invariant 45), a worker slot where there was a direct play. Fluster switches the track in mpv and pays nothing. Expected differences: tag spellings if Jellyfin compares strings, and OriginalLanguage if Jellyfin has none without a provider.
